ENGLISH ACTIVITIES — MOCK EXAM #12
====

GRADE: Grade 1
SUBJECT: ENGLISH ACTIVITIES
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. quickly
   B. happiness
   C. run
   D. blue

2. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a joining word
   B. Only an action
   C. Only a describing word
   D. A person, place, thing, or idea

3. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Many unrelated topics with no link
   B. One main idea with supporting sentences
   C. Only one word repeated
   D. No full stops

4. When practising Pre Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Pre Reading.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Pre Reading.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Pre Reading.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre Reading.

5. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the Library
   B. Where is the library
   C. where is the library
   D. Where is the library?

6. When practising Handwriting, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Handwriting.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Handwriting.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Handwriting.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Handwriting.

7. When practising Word Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Word Reading.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Word Reading.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Word Reading.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Word Reading.

8. When practising Attentive listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Attentive listening.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive listening.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Attentive listening.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Attentive listening.

9. When practising Language School, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Language School.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language School.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Language School.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Language School.

10. When practising Connected text and fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Connected text and fluency.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Connected text and fluency.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Connected text and fluency.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Connected text and fluency.

11. When practising Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Comprehension.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Comprehension.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Comprehension.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Comprehension.

12. When practising Phonics, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonics.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Phonics.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Phonics.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Phonics.

13. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goes
   B. going
   C. goed
   D. went

14. When practising Language Welcome and, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Language Welcome and.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language Welcome and.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Language Welcome and.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Language Welcome and.

15. When practising Pre-Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Pre-Writing.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Pre-Writing.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Pre-Writing.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre-Writing.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. In three clear sentences, explain Language Welcome and and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Language School and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Pre Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Phonics and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Word Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Connected text and fluency and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Comprehension and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

23. In three clear sentences, explain Pre-Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
